items.title: Follow-up: Validate spec for components
items.body:
https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/1745#note_2225729944

> We would need to modify the following struct;
> 
> ```go
> type specDef struct {
> 	Spec map[string]interface{} `yaml:"spec"`
> }
> ```
> 
> to have the value `Spec` be another struct.
> 
> The question here is, how flexible can `spec` be? If we accept any kind of structure then we can leave it as it is. But if it's a well-defined spec, it makes sense to define every field.

> we have a strict `spec` definition; https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/f89ee11b1f4649cd9c069728353c57f1008c971c/app/validators/json_schemas/catalog_resource_component_spec.json

<!-- implementation plan added during 2026-09 backlog triage -->

## Implementation plan

> **Note:** This plan was drafted during an AI-assisted triage of the backlog and has not been validated by a maintainer. Treat it as a starting point: file paths, line numbers, and the approach may need adjusting.

All work is in `internal/commands/project/publish/catalog/`.

1. **Model the spec.** In `publish.go`, replace the `Spec map[string]any` field on `specDef` ([publish.go:265](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/internal/commands/project/publish/catalog/publish.go#L265)) with `Spec *componentSpec`. Define `componentSpec` to mirror [`catalog_resource_component_spec.json`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/master/app/validators/json_schemas/catalog_resource_component_spec.json): `Inputs map[string]*componentInput` (`yaml:"inputs"`), `InputsOrder []string` (`yaml:"inputs_order"`), `Component []string` (`yaml:"component"`), `Description string` (`yaml:"description"`). Give `componentInput` `Default any`, `Regex string`, `Type string`, plus a catch-all for other keys: the schema closes only the top level, the per-input object is open.

2. **Add `validateSpec`.** Add `func validateSpec(componentName string, spec *componentSpec) error` and call it from `extractSpec` ([publish.go:270](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/internal/commands/project/publish/catalog/publish.go#L270)) after the YAML unmarshal. Check what the server schema can actually reject: `description` at most 256 characters, every `component` entry in `name`, `sha`, `version`, `reference` and unique, every `inputs_order` entry naming a key that exists in `inputs`. Wrap failures with `cmdutils.WrapError` and name the component and the offending field so the message points at the file.

3. **Keep unknown top-level keys non-fatal.** Decode unrecognised top-level keys into a catch-all map and report them as a warning through `iostreams`, not as an error. The schema is `additionalProperties: false` today but gained `inputs_order` after this issue was filed, so a hard rejection makes the CLI refuse specs the server accepts. This is the review point that stalled [!3648](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3648). Thread `*iostreams.IOStreams` from `Publish` into `publishToCatalogRequestBody` ([publish.go:145](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/internal/commands/project/publish/catalog/publish.go#L145)) and `extractSpec` so the warning has somewhere to go.

4. **Do not change the wire format.** `publishToCatalogRequestBody` copies the spec straight into the POST metadata. Use a pointer for `Spec` and `json:"...,omitempty"` tags on `componentSpec` so a component with no `spec:` block still serializes as `"spec": null` rather than `{}`, which is what the existing golden request body in `TestPublishCatalog` asserts for `component-2`.

5. **Tests.** Extend `publish_test.go`. Add a `Test_validateSpec` table with: a valid spec, `description` over 256 characters, an invalid `component` entry, an `inputs_order` entry with no matching input, and an unknown top-level key that must warn and pass. Add fixtures under `testdata/test-repo/templates/` only for a case you need end to end. `TestPublishCatalog`, `Test_fetchTemplates` and `Test_extractComponentName` must keep passing unchanged.

6. **Docs and checks.** No flags change, so `docs/source/repo/publish/catalog.md` needs regenerating only if you extend the `Long` text in `NewCmdPublishCatalog` to mention client-side validation. If you do, run `make gen-docs` and commit the regenerated page in the same commit. Finish with `make test` and `make lint`.

items.title: Follow-up from "fix(commands): fixes to commands and env vars"
items.body:
The following discussion from !2317 should be addressed:

- [ ] @hacks4oats started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/2317#note_2713626408): 

    > If we want to log to the `iostreams.IOStreams.StdOut`, we need to inject this new dependency here just for that. I suspect that checking env vars this deep inside of the program setup might be the wrong approach. Instead, the debug http setting should be parsed further up and propagated to the client.

/cc @faleksic

<!-- implementation plan added during 2026-09 backlog triage -->

## Implementation plan

> **Note:** This plan was drafted during an AI-assisted triage of the backlog and has not been validated by a maintainer. Treat it as a starting point: file paths, line numbers, and the approach may need adjusting.

Goal: read `GLAB_DEBUG_HTTP` once during program setup and propagate the resulting writer into the API client, instead of reading the env var inside `internal/api/client.go` and writing to `os.Stderr`. Merge request !3647 is a closed reference implementation for steps 1, 2, 4 and 5; it can be reused, with the review feedback on it applied and the gap in step 3 filled.

1. `internal/api/client.go`: add an exported `HTTPDebugConfig{Enabled bool; Writer io.Writer}` and a `WithHTTPDebug(HTTPDebugConfig) ClientOption` alongside the existing options (`WithProxy` at line 232 and neighbours), store it on `Client`, and replace the env lookup at line 214 with `if c.httpDebug.Enabled { rt = &debugTransport{rt: rt, w: c.httpDebug.Writer} }`. Give `NewClientFromConfig` (line 341) a trailing `options ...ClientOption` and append them after the config-derived options. Drop the now unused `utils` import.

2. `internal/cmdutils/factory.go`: read `GLAB_DEBUG_HTTP` in `NewFactory` (line 54), store the config on `DefaultFactory` with `Writer: io.StdErr`, expose it as `HTTPDebug() api.HTTPDebugConfig` on the `Factory` interface (line 23), and pass `api.WithHTTPDebug(f.httpDebug)` at the three `NewClientFromConfig` calls (lines 107, 136, 172). Do not add a `Writer != nil` guard: `IOStreams.StdErr` is always set for a properly constructed `IOStreams`, and the redundant check was a review point on !3647.

3. Cover the client construction sites that live outside the factory, or `GLAB_DEBUG_HTTP` silently stops working for them: `internal/commands/update/check_update.go:104`, `internal/commands/whatsnew/whatsnew.go:118` (both go through `CreateUnauthenticatedClient`), `internal/commands/artifactregistry/login/login.go:110`, and `internal/commands/auth/docker/artifact_registry.go:42` (the `Helper` already holds an `io` field). !3647 handled only the first two.

4. Update the other `Factory` implementations for the new interface method: `internal/testing/cmdtest/factory.go` (add an `HTTPDebugStub` field and getter) and the local `factory` in `cmd/gen-docs/docs.go`.

5. Tests: rework `TestDebugTransportIncludesCustomHeaders` in `internal/api/client_headers_test.go:152` to pass a `bytes.Buffer` through `WithHTTPDebug` instead of `t.Setenv` plus reaching into `debug.w`, and add a case asserting no `debugTransport` is installed when the config is disabled. Add a `NewFactory` test in `internal/cmdutils/factory_test.go` that sets the env var and asserts the resulting client writes request traces to the factory's stderr buffer. Assert observable behaviour, not `HTTPDebug()` field values: asserting on the config struct was the second review point on !3647.

6. No `cobra` help text changes, so `make gen-docs` is not needed; `GLAB_DEBUG_HTTP` stays registered in `internal/config/envvars.go:41` and documented in `docs/source/configuration.md`. Verify with `go test ./internal/api/... ./internal/cmdutils/... ./internal/commands/update/... ./internal/commands/whatsnew/...` and `make lint`.

items.title: Add tests for "fix: make SilentError exit with code 1 as documented"
items.body:
The following discussion from !1859 should be addressed:

- [ ] @michaelangeloio started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/1859#note_2316190416):  (+1 comment)

    > **non-blocking**: Curious if we should add a check for the exit with the new logic?

Add tests for:

1. returning from cmd with `SilentError` results in exit code 1 with no message
2. returning nil from cmd results in error code 0
3. returning any other error from cmd results in printing the error and error code 1

<!-- implementation plan added during 2026-09 backlog triage -->

## Implementation plan

> **Note:** This plan was drafted during an AI-assisted triage of the backlog and has not been validated by a maintainer. Treat it as a starting point: file paths, line numbers, and the approach may need adjusting.

The exit-code mapping is three lines of `main()`, so split the work: make the mapping
testable in-process, then pin the end-to-end behavior with one subprocess test.

1. In `cmd/glab/main.go`, extract the exit-code decision from the `if err := fang.Execute(...)`
   block (currently `cmd/glab/main.go:167-180`) into a package-level helper,
   `func exitCodeForError(err error) int`: return `exitError.Code` when `errors.As(err, &exitError)`
   matches `*cmdutils.ExitError`, and `1` otherwise. Replace the inline branch with
   `os.Exit(exitCodeForError(err))`. Behavior is unchanged, this only creates a seam.
2. Add `TestExitCodeForError` to `cmd/glab/main_test.go` as a table test covering ask 1 and
   ask 3 at the mapping level: `cmdutils.SilentError` returns 1, `fmt.Errorf("x: %w", cmdutils.SilentError)`
   returns 1, a plain `errors.New` returns 1, `cmdutils.WrapErrorWithCode(err, 2, "")` returns 2,
   and `cmdutils.CancelError()` returns 2.
3. Add `TestMain_ExitCodes` to `cmd/glab/main_test.go` for the process-level behavior, following
   the re-exec precedent already in the repo at `internal/config/flock_test.go:22-50` rather than
   building a binary from inside the test. Gate the child branch on an env var (for example
   `GLAB_TEST_MAIN_ARGS`): when it is set, the test sets `os.Args = append([]string{os.Args[0]}, strings.Fields(...)...)`,
   calls `main()`, and then calls `os.Exit(0)` explicitly so the child's status comes from `main()`
   and not from goleak's verification in `TestMain`. The parent runs
   `exec.Command(os.Args[0], "-test.run", "^TestMain_ExitCodes$")` per case with separate stdout and
   stderr buffers, and reads the status through `errors.As(err, &exitErr)` plus `exitErr.ExitCode()`.
4. Give the child a hermetic environment: `GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=<t.TempDir()>`, `GLAB_CHECK_UPDATE=false`,
   `GLAB_SEND_TELEMETRY=false`, `GLAB_NO_PROMPT=true`, `NO_COLOR=1`, and no `GITLAB_TOKEN`, so the
   run does not touch the developer's config, the network, or the update check.
5. Cover the three asks with commands that need no API call:
   `auth git-credential store` returns `cmdutils.SilentError` from
   `internal/commands/auth/login/helper.go:71`, so expect exit 1 with both streams empty;
   `version` returns nil, so expect exit 0; `config get` with no argument fails cobra's
   `ExactArgs`, so expect exit 1 with the arg-count message on stderr.
6. Verify with `go test ./cmd/glab/... -run 'TestExitCodeForError|TestMain_ExitCodes' -count=5` and
   `make test-changed`. No help text, flags, or command descriptions change, so `make gen-docs`
   is not needed.

Note for whoever picks this up: !3658 already targets the same three asks, but builds a `glab`
binary with `go build` from inside the test and adds roughly 230 lines of environment scrubbing.
Reviewing that MR down toward the lighter shape above is likely faster than starting over.
